name: Citizenship by Descent / Birth

requirements.blocker_text: Any person born in Venezuela acquires citizenship automatically, regardless of either parent's nationality or immigration status -- unconditional jus soli.

requirement_groups.name: Born abroad, both parents Venezuelan by birth

requirements.blocker_text: A child born abroad to two parents who are themselves Venezuelan by birth acquires citizenship automatically, no residence or declaration required.

requirement_groups.name: Born abroad, one parent Venezuelan by birth

requirements.blocker_text: A child born abroad to one parent who is Venezuelan by birth acquires citizenship if the child either resides in Venezuela, or declares the intent to hold Venezuelan nationality at a Venezuelan diplomatic mission.
requirements.fix_path: Establish residence in Venezuela, or make a declaration of nationality at a Venezuelan consulate/embassy.

requirement_groups.name: Born abroad, one parent naturalized Venezuelan

requirements.blocker_text: A child born abroad to a NATURALIZED (not birth-citizen) Venezuelan parent acquires citizenship if the child resides in Venezuela before turning 18, then formally declares the intent to hold Venezuelan nationality at the Ministry of Interior or Public Registry.
requirements.fix_path: Reside in Venezuela before age 18, then declare nationality at the Ministry of Interior or Public Registry.

evidence_required.document: Parent's proof of Venezuelan nationality (by birth or naturalization, as applicable)

sources.title: Wikipedia -- Venezuela's unconditional jus soli rule, and the tiered jus sanguinis conditions for children born abroad depending on whether the Venezuelan parent is a citizen by birth or by naturalization

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Venezuela). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to Wikipedia only (tier 4); Venezuela's 2004 Law of Nationality and Citizenship (Ley de Nacionalidad y Ciudadania) itself was not locatable/fetchable in this build from a government (mppre.gob.ve, saime.gob.ve) or gazette source -- worth a dedicated follow-up. GENUINE POSITIVE FINDING: unconditional jus soli (any birth in Venezuela grants citizenship, no parental-status conditions at all) is one of the most unrestricted birthright-citizenship rules built in this dataset, comparable to the U.S.'s constitutional birthright rule documented in this dataset's original 15-country build. The tiered jus sanguinis structure (full parents vs. one parent vs. naturalized parent, each with different conditions) is a genuinely more granular structure than most descent laws built elsewhere in this dataset. dual_citizenship_allowed set true per Article 34 of the Constitution (also cited in ve_citizenship_naturalisation.json).
